intent.note: Task clause: 'start that child with SIGINT reset to SIG_DFL (preexec_fn on POSIX; on Windows ... check)'. Diff: tools/gate-parity.py:1700-1708 adds _default_sigint() calling signal.signal(SIGINT, SIG_DFL); :1724-1725 passes it as preexec_fn only when os.name == 'posix' (None otherwise, so Windows never sees the POSIX-only argument). preexec_fn runs in the forked child before exec, so it cannot change the parent's disposition; the module has no threading/concurrent use (grep), so the preexec_fn thread-safety caveat does not apply. Acceptance (1): vsh13 (:1876-1895) sets SIGINT to SIG_IGN around both INT legs (the vsh6 kill leg and the vsh9 generator int leg), restores in finally, and asserts 130 for both with no 'resumed'/'status=' output and empty scratch. Acceptance (2)/(3 for this file): I ran python3 tools/gate-parity.py --selftest once from the task tree: 'ALL PASS: 71/71 cases passed', exit 0. The executor's outcome (reset in the one helper all vsh cases use; vsh13 added; 71/71 foreground and under nohup &) describes the diff. I did not re-run the nohup variant or the full sweep.
